title: Pegboard spool holder: the A1's active spool, on the board
subtitle: One arm straight out of the board, spool face parallel to the board · 2 shared hook pegs + 4 pins (tools/pegboard.py) · your Menards 3/16" board · X out from the board, Z up · mm

meshes.label: Spool holder (2 hooks side by side, 4 pins 2" and 3" below, arm, end lip)
Reference 1 kg spool: 200 OD × 68 wide, 53 bore
Your board: Menards 3/16" white (6.35 mm holes, 3.94 mm thick)

scale_note: Real size. Pegs are the shared 6.1 mm hooks + pins. The spool is a typical 1 kg spool (200 mm across, 68 mm wide, 53 mm bore); the arm and lip pass through bores down to 50 mm and hold spools up to 82 mm wide.
notes: v3: taller span and more pins. The hooks are now 3 holes (3") above the bottom pins instead of 2, a 50% longer lever against the spool pulling the part off the board. There's a second pair of pins 2 holes below the hooks, so 6 holes now take the load (2 hooks + 4 pins). The arm stays just under the hooks, so the spool hangs at the same height relative to the hook holes. It still hangs by rocking in: tilt it, push both hook tips up through the holes, swing the bottom in until all 4 pins drop in. Printing: on its side; one column of pegs is on the bed, and the other column (1 hook + 2 pins) needs tree supports. Still to check: (1) which holes behind the A1 (the spool stands 74 mm out from the board, so it must clear the bed's travel); (2) whether the filament reaches the A1's PTFE tube; (3) fixed arm OK, or a spinning hub on 608 bearings?
